newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klestil to leave hospital within week.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klestil to leave hospital within week.

text.p: Austrian President Thomas Klestil, admitted to hospital two weeks ago with a form of pneumonia, is expected to go home by the end of the week, doctors said on Sunday.

Klestil, 63, had made good progress from an unspecified acute lung inflammation, chief physician Professor Wolfgang Graninger told Reuters. The president would remain in intensive care until he left hospital to protect him from media intrusion and ensure adequate rest.
"Theoretically Klestil could take up his duties again now, but we have advised him to wait for a week or two to allow himself time to rest," Graninger said.

Klestil was unconscious for three days and hooked up to an artificial respirator last weekend following a deterioration in his condition. Graninger said it was not unusual to be unable to diagnose a specific type of pneumonia.
"He came in with a high fever, coughing and severe pneumonia. He showed an initial improvement but that did not last so he underwent a lung biopsy," Graninger said.

"We found no hint of the infectious agent, but the biopsy showed us his deterioration was caused by hypersensitivity of the immune system," he added. The president was put on a course of cortico steroids, which he was still taking.
Chancellor Franz Vranitzky took over as acting head of state last Monday at the request of the president.
Initial secrecy surrounding the president's illness had sparked media speculation he could have cancer or AIDs, which was swiftly denied by spokesmen.
"His condition was never life-threatening," Graninger said.
Klestil first sought medical attention in July this year, complaining of inflammation of his joints shortly after a trip to Turkey.
Under the constitution, the chancellor assumes the duties of president for 20 days, after which responsibilities pass, in turn, to the three presidents of parliament.
